content:
If this is an IMAP account, your email provider probably has a retention policy for its Spam folder and will automatically delete them after some period of time (30 days for Google, for example.)

You can set your own retention policy for that folder to be something shorter than the provider. Right-click on the folder name in the Folders List, choose "Properties", "Retention Policy" and choose your settings.

You're on the right track. I would use the add-on "ImportExportTools NG" (https://addons.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/addon/importexporttools-ng/) to export any emails you want to pass on the Outlook user. Be sure to set the ImportExportTools options to make sure it does what you want. Then you can export individual messages or entire folders to EML format. You will wind up with one or more folders on your computer filled with separate files, each representing one email message. You can transfer the whole lot to them using Dropbox or other method.

On their end, they can import them into Outlook by drag-and-drop for use. I found this recipe, which looks accurate to me:

https://www.clrn.org/how-do-i-import-emails-into-outlook/

Importing EML Files

EML files are commonly used for storing individual email messages. To import EML files into Outlook:

- Create a Destination Folder: Create a new folder in Outlook where you want to import the EML files. This can be a subfolder within your inbox or a separate folder in your Outlook data file.

- Locate EML Files: Locate the EML files on your local drive or external storage device.

- Drag and Drop: Select the EML files you want to import and drag them into the destination folder in Outlook.

- Import Process: Outlook will automatically import the EML files into the selected folder. The speed of the import will depend on the number and size of the EML files.

Note: If you have a large number of EML files, consider breaking them into smaller batches for import to improve performance and reduce the risk of errors.

- Check your message filters for rules that contain a blank conditional clause and eliminate those rules. They don't make good logical sense and they should never have been allowed in the first place.
